entries.test: Compare dated predictions of an imminent GPT-5 release with its actual release date.

entries.note: “I think” qualifies the imminent-release prediction.

entries.test: Public comparative evaluations and release reception would show whether GPT-5 substantially surpassed GPT-4 and impressed users.
entries.note: The exaggerated language accompanies a substantive comparative capability prediction.

entries.test: Public GPT-5 evaluations of instruction compliance and unintended or unsafe behavior would establish whether it remained difficult to control.
entries.note: The following sentences give the metaphor a concrete behavioral meaning.

entries.test: Public evaluations of GPT-5 on straightforward tasks would show the frequency of obvious errors and how predictably they occur.
Public instruction-following evaluations would show whether users can reliably anticipate GPT-5's successes and failures.
Public results on prior benchmark items and longer novel physical, psychological, and mathematical reasoning tasks would establish GPT-5's reliability.
entries.note: Longer scenarios specify an emphasis, rather than an antecedent condition.

entries.test: Public hallucination evaluations and comparative misinformation-generation tests would show frequency, ease of induction, and increased capacity to produce plausible falsehoods.
entries.note: The forecast includes a causal claim about misinformation risk.

entries.test: If GPT-5 has guardrails, public jailbreak and benign-request evaluations would establish whether they permit prohibited outputs and reject reasonable requests.
entries.note: The source leaves guardrail deployment conditional. “Alternate” also suggests a temporal pattern stronger than the stated tradeoff.

entries.test: Public integration tests would show whether GPT-5's natural-language output can directly and reliably drive databases or virtual assistants.
entries.note: The normalization drops “natural language” and “simply and directly,” broadening the claim to other output formats and integration methods.

entries.test: Public API documentation and integration evaluations would establish whether programmers can access GPT-5's models of discussed entities in a form that reliably feeds downstream processes.
entries.note: The normalization omits the qualification about reliably feeding downstream processes.

entries.test: Public evaluations of GPT-5 assistants and agents against user-confirmed intentions would establish whether intent mapping is sufficiently reliable for their tasks.
Public capability evaluations would establish whether GPT-5 alone can handle arbitrary tasks, including the concrete examples Marcus supplies.
entries.note: “By itself” defines the system being evaluated.

entries.test: Public unaided GPT-5 tests against Cicero, autonomous-driving evaluations, and broad household-robot demonstrations would test the three capability claims.
entries.note: “Versatile behavior” drops the much stronger comparison to Rosie the Robot.

entries.test: Public evaluations of brainstorming, drafting, and dependable performance across general tasks would test the substantive capability contrast.
entries.note: “Pastiche generator” is rhetorical, but the sentence also commits to practical capability claims.

entries.test: Public alignment evaluations and documented failures around GPT-5's release would establish whether reliable alignment remained unresolved.
entries.note: The next sentences specify the relevant failures; “critical” adds an evaluative description.

entries.test: Public GPT-5 evaluations against stated helpfulness, harmlessness, and truthfulness standards would establish the reliability of its compliance.
Dated public reports of previously concealed GPT-5 biases would establish whether discoveries occurred within days or months of release.
Public examples of GPT-5 advice demonstrably contradicting established facts or basic safety guidance would establish whether it gave clearly bad advice.
entries.note: In context, the claim concerns obvious advice failures rather than merely subjective taste.
The retrospective assessment is explicitly qualified by “may” and conditioned on AGI arriving.

entries.test: Public demonstrations and architectural disclosures would establish whether scaling LLMs alone can deliver trustworthy general intelligence.
entries.note: The surrounding paragraph identifies trustworthy general intelligence as the limit at issue.

entries.test: If trustworthy aligned AGI emerges, public architectural disclosures would show whether it uses the specified structure, built-in knowledge, and explicit reasoning and planning tools.
entries.note: “When it does” conditions the architectural prediction on the arrival of such AGI.

entries.test: Public research, investment, and deployed-system trends through July 27, 2035 would show whether the field shifted its focus toward integrating LLMs with other techniques.
entries.note: “Maybe much less” qualifies an earlier arrival, not the firm decade deadline.

entries.test: Retrospectives published by intellectual historians in 2043 would show whether they reach the stated conclusions about LLM overemphasis and a critical shift toward structured systems with deeper comprehension.
entries.note: “By 2043” changes “in 2043”; the normalization also omits the shift's gradual, critical character and deeper comprehension.
This expresses a conditional recommendation and hope, rather than predicting that the field will act.
“Shiniest” does not specify a ranking of model capability. The source questions an inference about an optimal path, without supplying a shared test for that path.

entries.test: Public demonstrations of trustworthy general AI and disclosures of its architecture would establish whether explicit knowledge and world models are required at its core.
entries.note: The surrounding discussion supplies the general-AI scope of “AI that we can trust.”

entries.test: Compare Marcus's December 2022 GPT-4 predictions with public GPT-4 evaluations and outcomes available when he made this retrospective assertion.
entries.note: Any predictions whose horizons were still open cannot yet support a blanket claim of demonstrated accuracy.
